claims.claim: IBM's structural thesis depends on converting enterprise demand for trusted hybrid-cloud/AI modernization into software, consulting and infrastructure revenue, with cross-division leverage from installed enterprise relationships and platform integration.

AI and quantum positioning can strengthen future capability, but the present causal bridge is weakened when legacy Infrastructure and Transaction Processing declines offset growth; successor bottlenecks include customer deployment economics, integration complexity and proof that AI demand produces incremental revenue rather than portfolio substitution.

causalEdges: enterprise AI/hybrid-cloud need -> IBM software/consulting deployment -> recurring platform/service revenue
installed enterprise relationships -> lower integration friction/cross-sell -> potential cross-division leverage
legacy segment decline -> portfolio drag -> weaker conversion of strategic AI growth into consolidated growth
falsifiers: AI demand grows while IBM's consolidated organic growth remains persistently weak because gains are offset by legacy declines or substitution.
Acquisitions and AI investment fail to improve durable cash generation after integration costs.
unknowns: incremental revenue directly attributable to current AI offerings

claims.claim: Strong AI/quantum narrative coexists with only modest reported Q2 top-line growth and declines in legacy segments; this is a material contradiction requiring downstream adjudication rather than a reason to reject the strategic thesis outright.
Raised expectations can be credible while still requiring follow-through; acquisition spending, debt and integration risk can dilute returns if AI/software growth does not outpace legacy drag.

contradictions.contradiction: Strong AI/quantum positioning versus modest Q2 revenue growth and declines in Infrastructure/Transaction Processing.
Raised full-year expectations versus weak reported Q2 top-line growth; requires subsequent-quarter follow-through.
